In this procedure, the provider applies the vasopneumatic device to an extremity for the purpose of reducing edema, or swelling. Explanation Vasopneumatic devices are a specialized form of equipment, which are designed to apply pressure to an extremity to reduce the swelling following an acute injury or surgical operation. In this procedure, the provider has the patient lie down on a table, and then the provider applies a sleeve or boot around the injured limb. He then uses a small compressor to fill this sleeve with air. He sets the compression machine in such a way that it causes the compression for a set period of time and then releases the pressure. He also places the part or limb being treated in an elevated position that aids in reduction of swelling. The provider may treat one or more areas in the same session.

In this procedure, the provider applies the paraffin wax on the joints or dips the limb in the paraffin wax solution. Explanation Paraffin bath is a physical therapy modality in which the provider uses the paraffin wax to treat a certain body area. Paraffin wax is a colorless semi??olid material derived from a petroleum product. The wax has a unique property of absorbing and retaining heat. In this procedure, the provider either applies the wax on the joint using a brush or he may dip the body part or limb in paraffin solution. This modality is most commonly used for treating wrist, hand, or knee joint pains and spasm caused by arthritis, or inflammation, of the joint. The provider may treat one or more areas in the same session.

The whirlpool method of treatment is a form of hydrotherapy that uses circulating water and air with varied temperature and pressure settings for the treatment of certain disorders. The whirlpool is a special bathtub with pumps placed at different points to produce and circulate air bubbles and water. The air bubbles and the circulating water massage the body and aids in improving blood circulation and range of motion. It is also a very effective method in the treatment of wounds such as ulcers, burns, and other such superficial abrasions. The whirlpool action cleans the wound of dead tissues, enhances blood circulation and relieves pain. A whirlpool may use cold or hot water, and it can be provided to the whole body or a single body area depending upon the necessity of the patient. Each session in the whirlpool may last from 10 to 30 minutes and may be provided once or twice daily. Explanation Under the guidance of a certified provider, the patient is partially immersed in a heated tank of a predetermined specific temperature. The water consisting of antiseptics is agitated, and this motion softens and loosens the dead tissue along with the drainage of debris, slough and necrotic tissues. This facilitates proper blood circulation and nutrition to the affected wound and promotes faster healing and pain relief. Read Less

The provider, who is typically a physical therapist, applies deep heat to specific body areas to reduce pain and increase blood flow to damaged tissues, muscles, and joints. Explanation There are three forms of diathermy that providers use to treat patients: shortwave, ultrasound, and microwave. In shortwave diathermy, the provider positions the body area to be treated between two condenser plates of the diathermy unit, directing the heat into subcutaneous tissues. Shortwave diathermy treats muscle and joint injuries. In ultrasound diathermy, which generates high frequency vibrations, the provider moves the diathermy unit across the body site to increase circulation. In microwave diathermy, the provider places an applicator on the body area to be treated. Microwave diathermy uses high frequency radiation to treat joint stiffness and other conditions.

In this procedure, the provider applies ultraviolet rays on one or more body parts to treat certain skin ailments. Explanation Ultraviolet therapy is a treatment technique that uses ultraviolet light to treat skin disorders like dermatitis or vitiligo. Ultraviolet rays are electromagnetic rays with shorter wavelengths. These rays have the unique property of improving the blood circulation in the affected area and to stimulate the production of collagen that repairs the damaged tissue. The provider delivers these rays through a fluorescent lamp. The provider may treat one or more areas in the same session. Terminology Vitiligo: Skin disease characterized by depigmented patches.

Electrical stimulation therapy uses electricity to stimulate the muscles for the treatment of pain and other disorders associated with muscles. Electrodes are placed on the affected muscle areas and an electric current of various intensity is passed through the electrode pads to expand and contract the muscles. This helps in the restoration of normal muscle strength, improved ability in the performance of activities, relief from pain, and improved blood circulation. Explanation Electrical stimulation acts as an electronic pain reliever. The provider applies a controlled amount of electrical stimulation (miniature pulse charges) over the skin or muscle which can be one of three modalities 3L, 3M or 3S (Low, Medium and Strong). In this procedure, the provider administers iontophoresis, which uses electric current to deliver medicine through skin. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minute session. Explanation Iontophoresis is the introduction of a drug through intact skin by application of electric current into the tissues of the body. Providers most commonly use it to treat hyperhidrosis (excessive sweating of the hands, feet, and underarms). The provider applies the electric current by placing the part to be treated in water and then passing electricity through the water, gradually increasing the current. The procedure works by plugging the sweat glands. Providers also use it to treat certain inflammatory conditions like bursitis and fasciitis. The provider may treat one or more areas in the same session. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minute session.

In this procedure, the provider uses a contrast bath for treating muscle soreness, swelling, and inflammation. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minute session. Explanation Contrast bath is also known as hot/cold immersion therapy. Providers use it to treat soreness, swelling, and inflammation in the joint or muscles. The technique involves immersing the joint or limb in the bath, alternating between hot and cold water to cause dilation and constriction of blood vessels respectively. This alternate dilation and constriction of blood vessels increases the circulation in the damaged tissue resulting in rapid recovery. The provider may treat one or more areas in the same session. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minute session.

Physical therapists use different treatment modalities that can help strengthen, relax, and heal muscles from their strained conditions. Explanation Physical therapists use Ultrasound machines that utilize high or low frequency sound waves in order to increase circulation to target areas. The sound waves are transmitted to the surrounding tissue and vasculature of the target area. In most instances a water bath or Ultrasound gel/lotion is required to be used in the facilitation of the process. The sound waves penetrate the muscles to cause deep tissue/muscle warming. This helps in tissue relaxation and removes muscle tightness. The warming effect also triggers vessel vasodilatation and increases circulation to the area that needs healing. Terminology Physical therapy modalities are a variety of treatment tools used by therapists to heal muscle related problems in a patient. Tips This modality is used primarily to treat inflammation of periarticular structures, neuromas, pain, muscle spasms, contractures, and to soften adhesive scars. Treatment would not be expected to exceed 4 treatments per week for longer than one month of time. Read Less

Explanation A Hubbard tank is a water tank in which the patient can perform underwater exercise. The provider uses this tank to deliver treatment through water. He has the patient submerge his extremities and trunk in the water. This therapy uses the buoyancy property of water to increase the range of motion of joints and hot water to reduce pain in the joints or muscles. The tank may also be fitted with an aerator that agitates the water and provides gentle massage and debridement of wounds. A Hubbard tank is especially useful in treatment of patients with extensive burns. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minute session.

The provider instructs and supervises the patient on aquatic therapeutic exercises for one or more areas of the body for a period of 15 minutes. Explanation The patient remains in direct contact with the skilled physical therapist at all times throughout the therapy. The physician demonstrates exercises and the patient follows their instruction and model to perform the same exercises while in the water. An array of specially designed instruments, like aquatic bikes, aquatic treadmills, and aquatic weights can be utilized based on patient's medical condition. Aquatic therapy refers to any therapeutic exercise, therapeutic activity, neuromuscular re??ducation, or gait activity that is performed in a water environment including whirlpools, hubbard tanks, underwater treadmills and pools. Therapeutic procedures are used in an attempt to reduce impairments and restore function through the application of clinical skills and/or services. The use of these procedures is expected to result in the improvement of the limitations/deficits in a reasonable and generally predictable period of time. The viscosity and buoyancy of water provides support to the patient's weight. This decreases the amount of weight bearing which reduces stress on the joints, helps in muscle strengthening, relaxes muscles and vasodilates vessels which increases blood circulation to the injured areas. Tips The total time of exercise can be divided into multiple units, each of 15 minutes, for billing purposes. If there are 5 time units in a single session of procedure, code for this 5 times. Explanation The provider may use a variety of techniques that include sharp debridement with scissors, forceps, or a scalpel (a surgical knife), or he may use a high??ressure waterjet, with or without suction. A licensed respiratory therapist or other non physician provider provides respiratory therapy in the patient?? home.



Explanation
The respiratory therapist provides respiratory therapy to patients with breathing disorders, such as emphysema, asthma, chronic bronchitis, and obstructive sleep apnea. Therapy can include administering oxygen and assessing oxygen levels, education on the use of nebulizers, and administering bronchodilators and advising the patient on the correct dosage to use. The provider may perform a respiratory assessment to determine the patient?? respiratory therapy needs, or a sleep apnea evaluation to determine if the patient suffers from sleep apnea. Other services may include training the patient on the use of CPAP equipment and care for a tracheotomy or tracheostomy. The respiratory therapist works with the physician to help the patient to avoid infections and complications of his condition.


Terminology
Asthma: Asthma is a disease that causes the airways of the lungs to swell and narrow, leading to wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing.

Bronchodilator: A substance, or medication, that increases airflow into the lungs by dilating the bronchi and bronchioles.

CPAP equipment: Continuous positive airway pressure therapy, or CPAP, which is a machine that increases air pressure in the patient?? throat. It is used to treat sleep apnea. The patient wears a mask that covers his nose and mouth or covers only the nose, with prongs that enter the nose.

Emphysema: A condition that causes bronchiole inflammation limiting airflow to the alveoli, or air sacs in the lung.  The disease causes lung tissue to lose its elasticity, destroys the alveoli, and causes bullae, or air filled sacs, to form on the lungs, which can rupture and cause the lung to collapse.

Nebulizer: A device that delivers drugs to a patient when he inhales medication that takes the form of a mist.

Obstructive sleep apnea: A condition that produces phases of shallow breathing and causes breathing to stop for several seconds while a patient sleeps. It narrows the airway or blocks it so that the patient does not receive enough oxygen, which causes him to awaken.

Tracheotomy: Incision into the trachea to open the airway. A tracheostomy, which is a hole or stoma in the trachea, can help the patient to breathe and may contain a tracheostomy tube.
